law: complete-ledger law (Mirror-Constrained BH Thermodynamics I §9 / III §4, N. Van Eeckhout): a varying result is not random but incomplete; residual variance is the share of omitted context and vanishes under full specification.
question: is the router's real-span variance (-38%..+67% across 3 holdouts) noise, or the signature of an omitted context factor?
omitted_factor_found: the ORACLE MARGIN available on the held-out tiers (how much the paths actually separate there)

per_holdout.reading: the only separable holdout — and the router does WORSE than the best single path
near-zero margin: '46% of almost nothing' — the ratio is meaningless here

conclusions: The variance was NOT noise: it is the omitted-variable signature of the held-out tiers' separability. Once counted, the picture is sharp.

The 'fraction of oracle ceiling' metric is ill-posed when the ceiling is near zero (a ratio whose denominator collapses) — the thermodynamic twin of a product that 'depends on mass' when a root is omitted. REPLACED by an absolute metric: AUC(router) - AUC(control), with the oracle lift reported alongside as the available margin.

The retrogradation of Rev20 STANDS, with a sharper diagnosis: not '~25% on average' (that number is a ratio artefact) but 'on the only separable holdout the learned router underperforms the best single path'. The router does not learn where there IS structure — from 8 training points.

The defect is the missing share of the ledger: the spans. ADR-007 Slice C (thousands of real spans with provenance) is the completion; the law predicts the defect closes if the context is complete, and says what to measure if it does not.
